findings.problem: Rule 1 (replace everyone) shows a red 'best lost' badge on S5, but the best solution of the population, S11 (1.0), is kept. A first-time learner can read 'best lost' as false: the lesson only says the best OLD solution S5 is lost.
findings.fix: Relabel the badge 'old best lost' (or 'S5 lost') and the caption 'Replace everyone: the old best can be lost.'
findings.evidence: s9@3 (badge beside S11 1.0 kept, caption 'the best can be lost')

findings.problem: Phase 2 switches from the plotted pair (1.1^n vs n^1.1) to n^2 vs 2^n at n = 60 without saying so. At n = 60 the red curve in phase 1 reads about 304 steps, yet phase 2 says 36 years for the 'exponential'. The learner may think the same red curve gives 36 years.
findings.fix: Add a short line 'a bigger exponential: 2^n' in phase 2, or caption 'At n = 60: n^2 takes microseconds, 2^n takes years.'
findings.evidence: s4@5 (red dot 97 at n=48) vs s4@10.5 (bars n^2 and 2^n)

findings.problem: The tag 'n = 60 · 10^9 steps a second' reads as the product n = 60 x 10^9, or as an equation for n. The meaning (n = 60 AND 10^9 steps per second) is lost.
findings.fix: Use a comma or two tags: 'n = 60' and '10^9 steps a second'.

findings.problem: '36 years' is Math.floor(36.53); the correct rounded value is 37, and the lesson and the outline give 36.5 years. The caption repeats '36 years'.
findings.fix: Show '36.5 years' (or 'about 37 years') in the tag and caption.
findings.evidence: s4@10.5 red tag, line 223 of the scene uses Math.floor

findings.problem: The closing tag 'hard: no fast exact method' states as fact what the lesson words as 'no known fast exact algorithm' (it is unproven). Scene 5's 'easy: fast and optimal' is true as written, so the pair is uneven.
findings.fix: Change to 'hard: no fast exact method known'.
findings.evidence: s6@11.5 red tag at the bottom; lesson l12-03.js 'No polynomial-time exact algorithm is known'

findings.problem: Caption 'An early cheap choice blocks cheaper ones later' is true (CD 5 fills C, blocking BC 7 and CE 6, both cheaper than the BD 8 taken), but the blocked cables BC and CE are not marked at frame 5 and 7, so the learner cannot see which cheaper ones were blocked. The data (blocked lists) is correct.
findings.fix: Mark the blocked cables with a red cross or red dashed line during steps 3 and 4 for about a second each (blocked = red role).
findings.evidence: s6@5 and s6@7 show only orange candidates; no blocked styling visible

findings.problem: The label flips to '30 items' at t = 5.0 while the counter is still rolling up from 64 (the frame shows 939,524,104 beside '30 items', with a 64-cell grid still shrinking). For about a second the number shown is not 2^30.
findings.fix: Change the item label when the count finishes (about 5.9), or roll the counter from 64 to 2^30 before the label changes.

findings.problem: The headline 'Every extra item doubles the work' does not cover the second half: the New York Tunnels count is 16 sizes per pipe (x16 per pipe), not doubling. The numbers themselves (16^21 = 1.9 x 10^25, 21 pipes, 16 sizes, 600 million years at 10^9 per second) are correct.
findings.fix: Optional: caption the pipes part 'More choices per item grow it even faster' or retitle 'Every extra choice multiplies the work'.

findings.problem: The recap's second card 'Hard problems blow up' is loose: the lecture says hard means the fastest KNOWN exact algorithm is exponential, and a big search space alone does not make a problem hard (sorting has n! orderings but is easy). The recap also never states the payoff of the title 'Why EAs?': approximate algorithms give good answers for hard problems without a guarantee. The third card only lists the loop.
findings.fix: Card 2: 'Hard: exact methods blow up'. Card 3: 'EAs: good answers to hard problems (select, vary, update)'.

findings.problem: Storyboard-vs-app disagreement the team should resolve: the app text in js/content/nic/l12-03.js (merge note, line 85) says S12 (0.2) does not get in, but pooling 12 and keeping the best 10 drops only S1 and S10 (0.1); S12 ties S4 at 0.2 and stays. The video (scene 9) is correct and gives mean 0.49; learners who read the lesson will see a contradiction.
findings.fix: Fix the app line to 'S11 and S12 both get in; S1 and S10 (0.1) drop out.' Do not change the video.
findings.evidence: s9@7 (S12 kept, S1/S10 gone); selfCheck merge.dropped = [S1, S10]; app line 85
